guarantees.claim: mux_sel_buf_output is continuously assigned to the type-cast (app_mux_sel_e) of mux_sel_buf_output_logic.
mux_sel_buf_err_check is continuously assigned to the type-cast (app_mux_sel_e) of mux_sel_buf_err_check_logic.
mux_sel_buf_kmac is continuously assigned to the type-cast (app_mux_sel_e) of mux_sel_buf_kmac_logic.
reg_state_valid_o is connected to the .out_o of u_prim_buf_state_output_valid, a prim_sec_anchor_buf instance whose .in_i is reg_state_valid and Width is 1.

assumptions.claim: mux_sel must always be a legal app_mux_sel_e encoding, because the type cast in the continuous assignments does not validate the input.
assumptions.risk: An out-of-range encoding could produce an invalid enum value, leading to undefined mux decode behavior and possible unintended data-path access.

assumptions.claim: The parameter AppMuxWidth must equal the actual bit width of the mux_sel signal.
assumptions.cond: when this chunk is synthesized or simulated
assumptions.risk: Width mismatch would cause silent truncation, expansion, or elaboration error, potentially corrupting the buffered mux select values and impacting secure path selection.

uncertain_points.claim: The same mux_sel signal fans out to three separate prim_sec_anchor_buf instances (producing mux_sel_buf_output, mux_sel_buf_err_check, mux_sel_buf_kmac) with SEC_CM: LOGIC.INTEGRITY commentary, but this chunk does not compare them nor enforce consistency. It is unclear whether downstream logic expects these three signals to always be equal and whether any discrepancy is detected. If mismatches are not handled, a single-point corruption in one buffer could silently propagate a wrong mux selection to part of the design.
uncertain_points.risk: An undetected discrepancy between the three buffered copies could allow an attacker to steer the KMAC engine, error-checking, or output path with a corrupted mux select, breaking the intended integrity scheme.
